title: Scratch a QR Code
tagline: Scratch a working QR code and it keeps scanning. Find the one scratch that finally breaks it.
description: An interactive lesson on why a QR code still scans after it is scratched: scratch a live code, watch its decoder find and fix the broken bytes, then scan it with a phone. Six small demos lead from squares and bytes to lines, curves and the 256-value number system behind Reed-Solomon error correction.
intro: A lesson on why a QR code still scans after a big chunk of it is scratched off. The code carries extra check bytes (numbers worked out from the message) that rebuild what is missing. For anyone who has scanned a scuffed code on a menu or a parcel: scratch the one below, then scan it with a phone.

makingOf: This page is an Opus cameo: it was built by a team of Claude Opus agents instead of the usual Sonnet team. Everything runs in your browser and nothing you type leaves your device. The code is drawn by the page’s own hand-written encoder (versions 1 to 6, levels L, M, Q and H) and read back after every scratch by its own decoder, which repairs bytes with Reed-Solomon error correction over the 256-value number system QR codes use. Before publishing, the page’s codes were checked against the standard’s worked example and against two independent open-source QR decoders reading screenshots of this page.
